questions.q: The ____ Model for New Normal in Education has been designed by many educational institutions.
questions.explanation: The Readiness Model was designed by educational institutions for the new normal, focusing on preparing learners, teachers and systems for remote learning.

questions.q: The most critical factor that plays a significant role in the success of any remote learning program is the ____.
questions.explanation: Readiness of the participants (learners and teachers) is the most critical factor for remote learning success; software and teacher personality matter less if participants are not ready.

questions.q: The typical picture of a teacher being a ____ of knowledge to the students has been replaced.
questions.explanation: The traditional image of the teacher as a dispenser of knowledge to students has been replaced by that of a facilitator who guides learners' own construction of knowledge.

questions.q: What does today's teacher need to be successful in the classroom?
questions.explanation: Today's teacher needs digital skills for technology-mediated teaching, life skills and communication skills, so all of these are required.

questions.q: Students who consider intelligence as a ____ entity tend to focus on their goals despite obstacles.
questions.explanation: Students who see intelligence as malleable (growth mindset) believe effort improves ability, so they keep focusing on their goals despite obstacles. Those who see it as fixed tend to give up when they hit difficulties.

questions.q: ____ feedback to students is important for learning.
questions.explanation: Useful feedback is clear, explanatory and timely: it tells students why something is right or wrong and how to improve while it still matters, so all the options apply.

questions.q: Students tend to enjoy learning and have better outcomes when their motivation is more intrinsic than extrinsic.
questions.explanation: True. Intrinsic motivation (learning for interest and satisfaction) is linked to greater enjoyment, persistence and better outcomes than learning only for external rewards.

questions.q: Long term goals are also called ____ goals.
questions.explanation: Long-term goals are called distal goals; short-term, near goals are called proximal goals.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a reward?
questions.explanation: Rewards can be social (clapping, compliments) or material (money), so all the options are examples of rewards.

questions.q: ____ is a teaching approach that generates feedback students can use to improve their performance.
questions.explanation: Assessment for learning (formative assessment) is used during teaching to generate feedback that students can use to improve their performance, rather than just to award marks.
